LESSON: READING 14.2.1 STUDY SKILLS: SUMMARISING

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 14
Topic 14.2: Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills: Summarising

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills: Summarising. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to summarise information?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the main ideas in texts
2. write a summary of ideas from varied texts
3. appreciate the importance of summarising information in a given context

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 14.2.1 STUDY SKILLS: SUMMARISING
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills: Summarising helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 14.2.1 STUDY SKILLS: SUMMARISING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the main ideas in texts

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the main ideas in texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the main ideas in texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills: Summarising”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the main ideas in texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Write a summary of ideas from varied texts

What this means
In this part you learn to write a summary of ideas from varied texts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: write a summary of ideas from varied texts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills: Summarising to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can write a summary of ideas from varied texts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the importance of summarising information in a given context

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of summarising information in a given context. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of summarising information in a given context.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of summarising information in a given context. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills: Summarising is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills: Summarising”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the main ideas in texts)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills: Summarising to a partner. (skill: write a summary of ideas from varied texts)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the importance of summarising information in a given context)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills: Summarising to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the main ideas in texts.
3. Practise this skill: write a summary of ideas from varied texts.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of summarising information in a given context.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills: Summarising from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills: Summarising: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills: Summarising?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to summarise information?
2. What factors should one consider when summarising an event?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 14.2.1 Study Skills: Summarising means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the main ideas in texts.
5. Be able to: write a summary of ideas from varied texts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
